sources.supports: updateDataset validates the dataset identifier, posts to update_dataset/{dataset_id} with the payload as the JSON body and parses the reply with DatasetSchema. The payload is passed through unexamined: no public method parses UpdateDatasetPayloadSchema, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.

UpdateDatasetPayloadSchema declares both name and variables optional and records that an empty body is intentionally allowed and forwarded, which TestRail treats as a no-op. The variables map is the same string-to-string form the creation payload takes.

update_dataset updates an existing dataset; its parameter table carries dataset_id alone, marked required, and the article states the request body has the same format as add_dataset and the reply the same format too. It does not state whether a supplied variables map replaces the dataset's values or merges into them. The documented 400 causes include an invalid dataset name, a dataset name that already exists in the project, and variable/value pairs containing invalid data such as a variable name that does not exist or values not submitted as strings. 403 covers insufficient project permissions, no add/edit permission for Test Data within the project, and "Not an Enterprise license/subscription".

input_policy.notes: The variables map is the documented extension point and its keys stay open; the payload's own fields do not, so an unknown field beside name and variables is refused, including the id the article's add_dataset example shows and its parameter tables never list. Whether a supplied map replaces or merges is TestRail's behaviour and is not documented, so this boundary neither claims one nor relies on it: it sends what the caller wrote.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the updated dataset in the get_dataset format, so the variables sent as a name-to-value map come back as an array of entries carrying server-assigned identifiers. Entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown body field, including the id the article's example shows and its parameter table does not document.
Accept an empty body and send it unchanged, which TestRail treats as a no-op, rather than refusing it locally or inventing fields to fill it.

parameters.semantics: The dataset to update. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as the only path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: No coercion. The JSON object is passed as the driver's second argument and sent unchanged. The object itself is required even though every field in it is optional, so a no-op is written out as an empty object rather than left implicit.

requirements.description: Preserve the object at driver argument 1 as the JSON request body.
Reject a body that is not an object before driver invocation.

parameters.semantics: A new name for the dataset. No coercion; TestRail owns the format and the uniqueness rule within the project.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
Send no name key when the caller did not supply one, so the dataset keeps the name it has.

parameters.semantics: The values this dataset gives the project's variables, keyed by variable name. Keys are open because they name instance data; every value must be a string, which is the rule TestRail states and refuses on.

wire.encoding: JSON object of string values under variables; keys are sent verbatim.

requirements.description: Preserve every key and value under variables, without renaming a key or reshaping the map into the array the reads return.
Accept a map of variable names to string values.

Reject a non-string value before driver invocation. It is the only one of TestRail's three stated rules about this map that is expressible here: that the variable name already exists in the project, and that a value is within its length limit, are both instance state this boundary cannot know, so those refusals arrive from TestRail.
Accept an empty map and send it rather than dropping the key, since dropping it would change what TestRail is asked to do.
Send no variables key when the caller did not supply one.
